title: Neighbors and community
theme: Borrowing, a noise feud, carrying things for each other, a block gathering, the stall keeper who knows everyone.

storylets.title: Can I borrow your ladder
storylets.note: A neighbor borrows a thing. Chain: nbr.tool-returned, or it quietly stays borrowed.

A.desc: an adult at a neighbor's door

b1: {A} knocks at {place} and stands back.
{A} raps on the door and waits with hands behind {A.his} back.
{A} knocks lightly, three taps.
b2: The door slides open. {B.desc} hands {A} a short folding ladder.
{B.desc} holds out a short ladder and a coil of rope. {A} takes both.
{B.desc} passes a folding ladder out through the door to {A}.
b3: {A} carries the load off down the block, the ladder knocking against the rail.
{A} hauls the ladder away from {place}, calling thanks over {A.his} shoulder.
{A} walks away with the ladder over one shoulder.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Take it, neighbor. Just bring it back before the weekend."
Overheard: {A} says: "What would I do without a {B.rel} like you?"
Overheard: {A} says: "You saved me again. Come by for buns on Sunday."

b1: {A} hauls a ladder along the block, a paper bag swinging from one rung.
{A} comes down the row with the folding ladder under one arm.
{A} walks up with the ladder held level, a bag hooked over one end.
b2: {A} hands the ladder back. {B.desc} checks the hinges twice.
{A} hands over a bag of sweets along with the ladder.
{A} holds out the borrowed ladder with a small bow. {B.desc} laughs.
b3: {A} and {B.desc} chat outside {place}, then {B.desc} points down the block.
{B.desc} says something that makes {A} grin. A short wave.
The two trade a few words in the doorway of {place}.

storylets.title: The knock after midnight
storylets.note: A noise complaint at a door. Chain: nbr.peace-offering, or a feud that never lands.

A.desc: an adult at a neighbor's door

b1: {A} bangs on the door of {place}, jaw tight.
{A} knocks hard and keeps knocking.
{A} pounds on the door, a hand on the frame.
b2: The door slides open. {B.desc} and {A} argue across the threshold.
{B.desc} snaps at {A} and {A} snaps right back. Voices carry.
{A} jabs a finger toward the ceiling. {B.desc} folds both arms.
b3: {A} stomps away from {place}.
{A} turns on {A.his} heel and goes off into the night.
{A} walks away shaking {A.his} head.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "Night after night, that drum! Some of us sleep at night!"
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Then knock like a person, not a hammer."

storylets.title: A plate on the step
storylets.note: Pays off the noise knock. A plate, a note, a nod.

A.desc: an adult at a neighbor's door

b1: {A} comes up to {place} carrying a covered plate.
{A} stops at the door of {place} with a cloth-covered dish in both hands.
{A} arrives with a plate under a cloth, shoulders stiff.
b2: The door slides open. {A} holds out the plate. {B.desc} takes it.
{A} hands the plate over with a few mumbled words.
{A} passes the dish across. {B.desc} peers under the cloth.
b3: {B.desc} nods slowly and says a few words. {A} lets out a breath.
{A} and {B.desc} talk. A hand goes out and gets shaken.
They speak low. The door stays open a while afterward.

storylets.title: A hand with the groceries
storylets.note: A younger neighbor carries bags for an older one.

b1: {B.desc} crosses the block slowly, a bag in each hand and a third over one arm.
{B.desc} climbs the sidewalk slope with two heavy bags, stopping every few steps.
{B.desc} makes {B.his} slow way along the block, the grocery bags dragging.
b2: {A} catches up and takes the bags without a word.
{A} jogs over, lifts the heaviest bag, and falls into step.
{A} relieves {B.desc} of the load and walks alongside.
b3: Both go into {place}. The door slides shut on a thank-you.
{A} follows {B.desc} into {place} with the bags.
{B.desc} unlocks the door, and {A} goes in with the groceries.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Thank you. You are a good {A.rel}."
Overheard: {A} says: "Anytime. That's what a {A.rel} is for."
Overheard: {A} says: "Anytime. Call down the hall. I will hear you."

storylets.title: Everybody on the stoop
storylets.note: A small block gathering. A good place for names and relations to leak out.

b1: {A}, {B.desc} and {C.desc} gather at the edge of the square with folding stools.
A little knot of neighbors forms around {A}, {B.desc} and {C.desc}.
{A} arrives with a pot; {B.desc} and {C.desc} are already unfolding stools.
b2: Bowls go around the circle. {C.desc} refuses seconds three times, then accepts.
{A} hands out mismatched bowls of stew.
{B.desc} breaks a bun and passes the pieces around.
b3: The circle talks over itself. {A} laughs at something {B.desc} says.
{C.desc} tells a long story. {B.desc} corrects the details.
Voices overlap. {A} points toward the roofs and the others turn.

log: Overheard: {C.desc} says: "{B.first}, you tell it. You were there."
Overheard: {A} calls: "{B.first}! Bring the salt."

storylets.title: The usual, by name
storylets.note: A shopkeeper who knows the regulars. The best way for a first name to leak out, verified by a loyalty card.

b1: {A} steps up to the counter without looking at the board.
{A} reaches the stall and holds up two fingers.
{A} gets to the front and says nothing. The stall keeper nods.
{A} arrives at the counter and puts coins down.
b2: {B.desc} serves {A} before the order is even spoken.
{B.desc} already has the cup out. {A} grins.
{B.desc} slides a bowl across the counter before {A} gets a word out.
{B.desc} serves {A} and adds a small extra.
b3: {A} and {B.desc} trade three sentences about the weather and the price of noodles.
{B.desc} asks a question; {A} waves a hand and answers.
They chat over the steam for a minute.
{B.desc} laughs at what {A} says and wipes the counter.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says: "There you go, {A.first}. Same as always."
Overheard: {B.desc} calls: "{A.first}! Your stool's open."
The stall keeper starts an order for {A} before {A.he} says a word.
The stall keeper has a cup out for {A} before {A.he} reaches the counter.

storylets.title: This one is for next door

b1: A delivery bot leaves a small parcel outside {place}. {A} comes out and picks it up.
{A} takes a parcel from a delivery bot and squints at the label.
A delivery bot sets a package down by the door of {place}. {A} lifts it.
b2: {A} walks the parcel next door and knocks.
{A} raps on the next door down, the parcel under one arm.
{A} knocks once and waits.
b3: The door slides open. {A} hands the parcel to {B.desc} and shrugs.
{A} holds out the parcel. {B.desc} takes it and bows.
{A} hands over the package and points the way the bot went.

log: The label reads {B.full}, in small print.
The parcel is addressed to {B.full}.

storylets.title: Something hot for the new tenant
storylets.note: A neighbor brings food to someone who just moved in. Uses the game's own new-neighbor flag.

A.desc: an adult with a covered dish

b1: {A} carries a covered dish across the landing.
{A} comes down the row with a steaming pot held in a towel.
{A} walks up to {place} with a plate and a spoon.
b2: {A} knocks and waits, straightening {A.his} collar.
{A} raps on the door and stands back with the dish held forward.
{A} knocks twice. A voice answers faintly.
b3: The door slides open. {A} hands the dish to {B.desc} and says a few words.
{A} hands over the dish. {B.desc} bows and takes it with both hands.
{A} passes the food across the threshold.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says: "You are the first one to knock. Thank you, neighbor."
Overheard: {A} says: "Welcome. I'm your {A.rel}, just across the hall."
Overheard: {A} says: "Welcome to the block. I live right across the hall if you need anything."

storylets.title: The pots along the wall
storylets.note: A neighbor waters potted plants on the block; another passes and speaks.

b1: {A} crouches by a row of potted plants and tips a cup of water into each.
{A} waters a vine climbing a pipe, a little at a time.
{A} kneels by a planter and pours slowly, pinching off a brown leaf.
b2: {B.desc} comes along the sidewalk with a bag and slows down.
{B.desc} walks up the block and stops to look.
{B.desc} passes the corner, then turns back.
b3: {B.desc} says something about the plants. {A} shrugs and answers.
{A} and {B.desc} talk over the pots. {B.desc} laughs.
{B.desc} crouches beside {A}, and the two argue softly over a yellow leaf.

log: {A} waters these pots: {seen} mornings on the feed.
{A} tips water into the planter again: {seen} mornings now.

storylets.title: Two doors, one conversation
storylets.note: Neighbors trade talk across a landing. Conversations carry names and news.

A.desc: an adult chatting at a door

b1: {A} leans in the doorway of {place} while {B.desc} stops alongside.
{B.desc} halts outside {place}, bag on one hip.
{A} stands in the doorway as {B.desc} hovers by the rail.
{A} and {B.desc} meet at the landing.
b2: They talk about the noise from the lift and the price of broth.
{A} points down the block, and {B.desc} shakes {B.his} head.
{B.desc} says something low and {A} laughs.
The two of them gossip for ten minutes, hands moving.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "They are putting a new stall on the corner. Rent is going up, mark my words."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "I heard the lift will be closed all of Thursday."

storylets.title: Soup at the door
storylets.note: Someone is sick at home, which the watcher can't see: the door just stays shut. Then a neighbor turns up with food, and the reason comes out on the step. Engine: a sick day is a routine change (the person stays home); this storylet only fires while it lasts.

b1: {B.desc} comes up the block holding a covered bowl level with both hands.
{B.desc} heads for {place} with a covered bowl, steam escaping from under the lid.
{B.desc} picks {B.his} way along the sidewalk, a lidded bowl held close.
b2: {B.desc} knocks twice and waits, the bowl balanced on one palm.
{B.desc} knocks at {place}, then once more, softer.
{B.desc} knocks with an elbow, both hands full.
b3: The door slides halfway open. {A} comes out, a blanket pulled around {A.his} shoulders.
{A} comes out of {place} in a long cardigan, hair flat on one side.
The door slides open. {A} steps out slowly, one hand on the frame.
b4: {B.desc} hands over the bowl. {A} holds it to {A.his} chest.
{B.desc} passes the bowl across. {A} takes it with both hands.
{B.desc} holds out the bowl. {A} takes it and nods.
b5: {A} goes in with the food. The door slides shut.
{A} goes back into {place}. The door slides shut on the steam.
{A} steps in and the door slides shut.
b6: {B.desc} heads off down the block, hands in pockets now.
{B.desc} walks away toward the corner without looking back.
{B.desc} continues down the sidewalk, lighter by one bowl.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Your door's been shut two days running. Eat this while it's hot."
Overheard: {A} says: "It's just a fever. Two days. I'll live." {B.desc} says: "Eat anyway."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Heard you were sick. Don't argue, just eat."
Overheard: {A} says: "You're a good {B.rel}. I mean it."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "What's a {B.rel} for? Bang on the wall if you need anything."
